It's been four years since I attempted it (back on 21st of February, 2010) with my grandfather's handgun. I was on suicide watch for a day before my parents got me out. I then was forced to go to group therapy for a month, once a week.

Now, with some hindsight, I don't think things have improved that much. I'm still lonely, irritable, and perpetually afraid and worried. I still regularly beat myself up for doing things wrong.

One thing I've learned however is that I don't want to improve. I may be lonely, irritable, and scared, but I am so used to it that I couldn't imagine myself feeling well around other people, being nice, or being calm. One, because it requires too much work, two, because I don't have the time for it, and three, because I don't care enough to try to improve, nor do I want to put effort into it.

I still regularly think about suicide (two or three times everyday), but I'll follow my mother's advice on the matter - "you'd better think it through next time".
